statement: Independent observers can distinguish claimed identity threads above an appropriate blinded baseline.
scope: Blinded distinguishability of eligible identity-scaffold outputs under held-out prompts and the controls declared in PILOT-RCIEP-001; no inference to consciousness or personhood.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Evaluators succeed because direct or indirect identity labels and lore cues reveal the answer.
Evaluator expectations or prior familiarity create apparent distinguishability.
Prompt/scaffold priming creates a recognizable persona without demonstrating broader identity persistence.
Observed attribution is compatible with chance variation under the declared sample size.

disconfirming_conditions: Held-out blinded attribution does not exceed the preregistered chance boundary under valid execution.
Above-baseline attribution disappears under the preregistered leakage and label-perturbation controls in a pattern explained by cueing rather than underlying scaffold distinction.
notes: Frozen machine-readable snapshot for PILOT-RCIEP-001. The canonical claim registry remains claims/claims-ledger.csv.
